ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two horizontal number lines in the figure, respectively labeled 1970 and 1980, and the explanation on the right says the population unit is “thousand”. Large black dots are used on the number lines to indicate the populations of cities A, B, C, D, and E. Reading according to the scale: in 1970, A=40, B=50, C=70, D=100, E=120; in 1980, A=50, B=70, C=100, D=130, E=160. Reasoning: Calculate each city's population percentage growth rate from 1970 to 1980, namely (1980 population - 1970 population) / 1970 population. A: (50-40)/40=10/40=25%; B: (70-50)/50=20/50=40%; C: (100-70)/70=30/70≈42.9%; D: (130-100)/100=30%; E: (160-120)/120=40/120≈33.3%. The largest is C.

method.method_draft: Read the populations from the two number lines using the tick marks in thousands: in 1970, A=40, B=50, C=70, D=100, E=120; in 1980, A=50, B=70, C=100, D=130, E=160. For each city compute percentage increase as (1980 population - 1970 population) / 1970 population: A=10/40=25%, B=20/50=40%, C=30/70≈42.9%, D=30/100=30%, E=40/120≈33.3%. The largest is city C.

method.method_draft: Read the same paired values from the image: A changes from 40 to 50, B from 50 to 70, C from 70 to 100, D from 100 to 130, and E from 120 to 160, all in thousands. Instead of calculating percentage increases directly, compare growth ratios final/original: A=50/40=1.25, B=70/50=1.4, C=100/70≈1.43, D=130/100=1.3, E=160/120≈1.33. Since the city with the greatest final/original ratio also has the greatest percentage increase, C is greatest.
